description: From the Cuatro Postes monument across the river you get the classic postcard view: the long crenellated wall of Ávila, its round towers and the Puerta del Alcazar gate washed in warm golden floodlight against the dark cloudy sky. Behind the ramparts the apse of the cathedral pushes into the wall line, a reminder that the church is part of the fortification. The foreground hillside is dark, the city beyond the walls a sparse scatter of lights under thin broken cloud.

prompts.prompt-r1.txt: Photorealistic artistic interpretation of the medieval walls of Avila, Spain, at night, viewed from the Cuatro Postes viewpoint outside the walls. The long crenellated Romanesque wall with its round towers and the Puerta del Alcazar gate glows warm under floodlighting against a cloudy night sky; the cathedral apse rises behind the walls. Dark foreground hillside, a few scattered city lights. No identifiable people prominent. Subject centred so it survives a 4:5 centre crop. No text or brand logos anywhere in the image, no on-image text at all.
